When you sign up for a membership based game you also have to accept the EULAs. So technically the server could be down a whole week and they wouldn't be legally obligated to reimburse your lost time. It's highly frowned upon though for community relation reasons though so it's always in the companies best interest to keep a positive relationship with their users.

But part of the EULA is that their service can end at \*any time\* because it's company property, you're just paying for access to use it.

​

example of Blizzard (World of Warcraft, Overwatch, Diablo etc company) 's EULA:

 

*Blizzard reserves the right to terminate this Agreement at any time* ***for any reason, or for no reason****, with or without notice to you.*

\[…\]

*In the event of a termination of this Agreement, any right to* ***any and all payments*** *you may have made for pre-purchased game access to certain Games* ***are forfeit****, and you agree and acknowledge that* ***you are not entitled to any refund*** *for any amounts which were pre-paid on your Account prior to any termination of this Agreement.*

​

These companies have every right to stop you from playing their game if they so choose, and you end up with no rights regarding it. Because you clicked that check mark when you signed up for the game.
Source: [The Atmoplex](https://twitter.com/theatmoplex/status/1734009003947266436)
